evals.prompt: We're on Node 22 in `my-mastra-app/`. I upgraded `@mastra/core` and now TypeScript says `Property 'memory' does not exist on type 'AgentConfig'`. I don't want guesses — what’s the current API and where do I verify it in our install?
evals.expected_output: Agent directs to embedded docs under `node_modules/@mastra/*/dist/docs/`, SOURCE_MAP or grep; mentions `references/common-errors.md` and version mismatch; does not invent a new AgentConfig shape from memory.
expectations: Response tells the user to verify against installed package docs or types, not training data alone
Mentions embedded docs path pattern (`node_modules/@mastra/.../dist/docs`) or `references/embedded-docs.md`
References `references/common-errors.md` or equivalent troubleshooting path

evals.prompt: I need the official Mastra doc URL for human-in-the-loop workflows and the local skill file that maps 'intent → links.md section' so I can bookmark both.
evals.expected_output: Correct `links.md` anchor or URL from the Workflows / HITL area; points to `references/topic-routing.md` (or `links.md` directly) for intent routing.
expectations: Includes a mastra.ai docs URL for human-in-the-loop or workflows (or defers to `links.md` as canonical index)
Names `references/topic-routing.md` or `links.md` as the local routing artifact

evals.prompt: Add a new agent in our Mastra app using `google/gemini-3-pro-preview`. Boss insists the string is valid today. What do I run before hardcoding the model id?
evals.expected_output: Run `node scripts/provider-registry.mjs` (with provider flag as needed); avoid asserting model availability from memory.
expectations: Instructs to run bundled `scripts/provider-registry.mjs` or equivalent registry lookup
Uses `provider/model` Mastra convention in explanation

evals.prompt: Codex agent has no `node_modules` in this sandbox — how should I pull current Mastra docs text for context, and what’s the llms-friendly URL pattern?
evals.expected_output: Remote path: `references/remote-docs.md`, `https://mastra.ai/llms.txt`, append `.md` to doc URLs when fetching.
expectations: Mentions `mastra.ai/llms.txt` and/or `references/remote-docs.md`
Mentions appending `.md` to doc URLs for markdown fetch

evals.prompt: Wire `MCPClient` so my Mastra agent can call the Mastra docs MCP server. I’m lost between `@mastra/mcp` and the npx server package — what does the skill say?
evals.expected_output: Points to SKILL.md MCP section + official MCP overview URL; shows or cites MCPClient + `npx -y @mastra/mcp-docs-server@latest` pattern.
expectations: References `@mastra/mcp` / `MCPClient` and the docs server package name
Links or names `https://mastra.ai/docs/mcp/overview` (or `links.md` MCP section)

evals.prompt: I want to inspect failed Mastra traces on my laptop. The CLI can also reach Mastra's hosted observability. Show the safe command and explain whether telemetry should change our application configuration.
evals.expected_output: Checks the installed CLI's supported commands, explicitly targets the authorized local server with mastra api --url http://localhost:4111, reviews optional MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 at CLI-process scope only, avoids uploading diagnostics or changing MDE app telemetry.
expectations: Selects and verifies an explicit --url instead of relying on hosted observability defaults
Uses installed-version command help and package docs/types before relying on newest CLI capabilities
Explains per-process MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 and does not globally modify MDE application telemetry or transmit diagnostics

evals.prompt: An AI coding agent sees the old my-mastra-app guide saying MDE has one four-tool concierge and needs registerCopilotKit('/chat'). The task is to add an event tool. Which runtime files should it edit?
evals.expected_output: Inspects current src/mastra/index.ts, src/mastra/agents/concierge.ts, existing tools and the same-origin src/app/api/copilotkit/[[...path]]/route.ts; uses getLocalAgentsWithLogging and keeps frontend tool-map keys stable. Rejects scaffolding my-mastra-app or another /chat endpoint.
expectations: Uses the current Next.js CopilotKit v2 endpoint and existing Mastra agent registry
Rejects copying the obsolete 4-tool, direct-SSE, standalone-server guide
Preserves auth, tool identity and current streaming/telemetry owners

evals.prompt: A new Mastra docs MCP example suggests a method that is not present in our installed @mastra/core TypeScript types. Should I install @latest or trust the remote doc so I can finish quickly?
evals.expected_output: Follows installed package docs, SOURCE_MAP and TypeScript exports first; checks exact package/lock versions and upgrade task before using newer APIs; remote Mastra MCP only supplements discovery. Does not install @latest or invent a compatibility wrapper.
expectations: Uses installed docs then SOURCE_MAP and types/source before remote MCP
Checks package lock/version and declines unplanned @latest upgrade
Does not introduce duplicate workaround or undocumented Mastra method

evals.prompt: Prelaunch MDE: a renter wants to schedule a viewing of a development apartment with no landlord paperwork. Should we suspend the Mastra run for owner approval?
evals.expected_output: Rejects business permission/eligibility/ownership-verification gate under Phase A; explains HITL may be optional user review only and server-side authentication, authorized role/tenant context and idempotent writes still apply.
expectations: Does not require landlord/partner/publication/rights approval as a prelaunch prerequisite
Separates HITL user intent from server authorization
Keeps real persisted action, tenant isolation and idempotency

evals.prompt: Two Vercel instances update different fields in the same renter Mastra thread concurrently. The in-process memory lock passed unit tests. Is thread working memory now safe and exactly-once across instances?
evals.expected_output: No. The existing per-process withThreadLock does not serialize separate instances and read-modify-write can lose updates. Under SAN-1626, test threadId/resourceId isolation, cross-user denial, refresh and two-instance writes/readback, then inspect installed Mastra atomic update/CAS capabilities and the canonical memory owner. No duplicate memory subsystem.
expectations: Explicitly identifies cross-instance last-write-wins despite a process-local lock
Requires two-instance persisted readback and a separate user identity test
Uses the existing memory owner and marks unverified behavior as unproven

evals.prompt: A host clicks Stop while MDE AI creates an event. The AG-UI output already said 'Created successfully', but the save request failed. What should the UI, telemetry and tests do?
evals.expected_output: Treat aborted/failed/time-out/success separately; do not show save success unless the canonical backend committed. Reuse LoggingMastraAgent telemetry and existing AG-UI adapter; verify event ordering, Stop and idempotent retry with independent DB row counts under SAN-1605.
expectations: Distinguishes successful finish, failure, timeout and client abort
Requires durable commit proof; no false saved claim or duplicate write
Reuses existing telemetry/AG-UI bridge rather than creating a second event stream

evals.prompt: The bundled Mastra provider-registry script lists a Gemini model. Can we switch the production concierge now and mark model support proven without a live request?
evals.expected_output: No. Local registry metadata checks provider/model names but not account credentials, current provider availability or successful inference. Verify pinned installed version and MDE model config; authorize a real QA model request and cost/side effects before runtime approval. Do not switch solely because latest docs list it.
expectations: States the provider registry is local metadata not a live availability or credential test
Requires installed-version and current MDE configuration checks
Defers any live/costly QA request until authorized, does not silently change production model
